declarations.name: PerspectivePanel
declarations.summary: Perspective workspace whose data connection and layout are configured by a serializable prop.

attributes.name: themes
attributes.description: Theme names offered by the status-bar picker; light/dark map to Pro Light/Pro Dark.

attributes.name: autosize
attributes.description: Auto-size mode (on by default); disable to drive resizes imperatively.

attributes.name: autopause
attributes.description: Auto-pause rendering while the element is not visible (on by default).

attributes.name: throttle
attributes.description: Render throttle in milliseconds; unset restores adaptive throttling.

attributes.name: settings
attributes.description: Whether the settings sidebar is open.

events.name: perspective-click
events.description: Fires when a plugin's grid or chart is clicked, with the clicked row and a `config` whose filters reproduce it.

events.name: perspective-select
events.description: Fires when a plugin's selection changes, with the configs whose filters to insert and remove.

events.name: perspective-global-filter
events.description: Fires on a master panel's selection, before it is applied to the global filter set.

events.name: perspective-global-filter-update
events.description: Fires whenever the global filter set changes, with the new `Filter[]`.

events.name: perspective-config-update
events.description: Fires after a panel's view config changes, with a deferred `getConfig()` accessor valid only during dispatch.

events.name: perspective-toggle-settings
events.description: Fires after the settings sidebar opens or closes, with the new open state.

events.name: perspective-statusbar-pointerdown
events.description: Fires with the original `pointerdown` as its detail when the status bar is pressed.

events.name: perspective-table-delete
events.description: Fires after a panel's `Table` is deleted and the panel unloaded.

events.name: perspective-active-panel-update
events.description: Fires when the active panel changes, with its id or `null` at zero panels.

events.name: perspective-command
events.description: Fires when the user picks a command declared through `setCommandSchema()`, with its `key` and context.

events.name: perspective-agent-tool
events.description: Fires when the agent invokes a tool, with a JSON string of `{name, args}` as its detail.

events.name: perspective-ready
events.description: One-shot: the panel connected, loaded its tables, and applied and rendered its initial workspace config.

events.name: perspective-error
events.description: A config apply failed (connection, mirror, or restore); detail carries the error.

events.name: perspective-copy-error
events.description: A keyboard copy (Ctrl+C or Cmd+C in a grid) was rejected by the viewer's copy: nothing is selected, or the clipboard write failed or was denied. Detail contains message and error; applications choose their notification UI.

members.name: setPluginConfigDefaults
members.description:
Merge `defaults` into the `plugin_config` defaults every
`<perspective-viewer>` on the page applies.

```javascript
customElements
    .get("perspective-viewer")
    .setPluginConfigDefaults({ group_pad: 10 });
```

parameters.name: defaults
parameters.description:
Values keyed like `plugin_config`, where `null` removes
a default, or `null` to clear the slot.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `plugin` limits the defaults to one plugin.

members.name: getPluginConfigDefaults
members.description:
The `plugin_config` defaults set by `setPluginConfigDefaults()`, one
entry per slot.

type.text: Promise<Array<{ plugin?: string; defaults: Record<string, unknown>; }>>

members.name: setColumnConfigDefaults
members.description:
Merge `defaults` into the `columns_config` defaults every
`<perspective-viewer>` on the page applies.

```javascript
customElements
    .get("perspective-viewer")
    .setColumnConfigDefaults(
        { date_format: { timeZone: "UTC" } },
        { type: "datetime" },
    );
```

parameters.name: defaults
parameters.description:
Values keyed like one `columns_config` entry, where
`null` removes a default, or `null` to clear the slot.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description:
`plugin` limits the defaults to one plugin, `type` to
columns of one view type.

members.name: getColumnConfigDefaults
members.description:
The `columns_config` defaults set by `setColumnConfigDefaults()`, one
entry per slot.

type.text: Promise<Array<{ plugin?: string; type?: ColumnType; defaults: Record<string, unknown>; }>>

members.name: saveWorkspace
members.description: Save the whole workspace with retained_panel_configs_by_table metadata after queued work completes.

members.name: save
members.description: Compatibility workspace save using legacy closed_channels metadata.

members.name: copy
members.description:
Copy this viewer's `View` or `Table` data to the system clipboard from
within a user gesture, rejecting if nothing could be written.

# Arguments

- `method` - The `ExportMethod` (serialized as a `String`) to use to
  render the data to the Clipboard.

# JavaScript Examples

```javascript
myDownloadButton.addEventListener("click", async () => {
    await viewer.copy();
})
```

members.name: export
members.description:
Exports this viewer's internal [`View`] as a JavaSript data, the
exact type of which depends on the `method` but defaults to `String`
in CSV format.

This method is only really useful for the `"plugin"` method, which
will use the configured plugin's export (e.g. PNG for
`@perspective-dev/viewer-charts`). Otherwise, prefer to call the
equivalent method on the underlying [`View`] directly.

# Arguments

- `method` - The `ExportMethod` to use to render the data to download.

# JavaScript Examples

```javascript
const data = await viewer.export("plugin");
```

members.name: setCommandSchema
members.description:
Set the function that declares this viewer's custom commands, replacing
any previously set, and re-query every plugin's command buttons when it
or its scopes changed.

# Arguments

- `schema` - A synchronous function from a command context to a `{
  commands }` list, or `null` to remove the current one.
- `options.scopes` - The surfaces the schema is evaluated for,
  `["context-menu"]` when omitted.

# JavaScript Examples

```javascript
await viewer.setCommandSchema(
    (ctx) => ({
        commands: [{ kind: "Command", key: "hello", label: "Hello" }],
    }),
    { scopes: ["context-menu", "datagrid-row"] },
);
```

members.name: agentConfig
members.description:
Configure the embedded LLM agent (see `prompt()`), replacing any prior
configuration and conversation.

The agent core is provider-agnostic: one OpenAI-chat-completions
protocol over primitive connection fields. Exactly one of
`config.url` or `config.engine` is required; the `providers` presets
exported by this package are plain spreadable collections of these
fields (`{...providers.anthropic, apiKey}`).

- `config.url` - a full chat-completions endpoint URL (any
  OpenAI-compatible service: Anthropic/Gemini compatibility endpoints,
  LM Studio, Ollama, OpenRouter, a proxy...).
- `config.engine` - an in-page engine object with an OpenAI-compatible
  `chat.completions.create(request)` method (e.g. WebLLM's `MLCEngine`);
  mutually exclusive with `url`.
- `config.headers` - extra request headers, sent verbatim.
- `config.apiKey` - sugar for the `Authorization: Bearer` header.
- `config.model` - model id sent with each request; local servers and
  engines generally answer with whatever model is loaded.
- `config.name` - cosmetic label for the chat badge (presets set this).
- `config.systemPrompt` - extra system-prompt context appended to the
  agent's built-in instructions.
- `config.maxTurns` - max model turns (tool-call rounds + the final
  answer) per `prompt()` call. Defaults to 16.
- `config.docs` - the agent metadata bundle, which supplies the
  `search_docs` corpus and the rich tool parameter schemas: the packaged
  `dist/docs/perspective-docs.json` asset as a parsed object (`import
  docs from "…json" with { type: "json" }`), a `fetch()` `Response`, an
  `ArrayBuffer`, a JSON string, or a `Promise` of any of those — and/or
  an inline array of `{title?, text}` entries for host data definitions.
  Omitted, `search_docs` searches an empty corpus and the parameter
  schemas degrade to permissive objects.
- `config.systemRole` - where the preamble (plus `systemPrompt`) is
  placed: `"system"` (default) or `"user"`. Some engines refuse a system
  message alongside `tools` because they substitute their own — WebLLM's
  Hermes function calling throws `CustomSystemPromptError` on ANY system
  message — and those need `"user"`, which folds the same text into the
  opening user turn.
- `config.entitlements` - access grants limiting which tools the agent
  is offered (and may call): any of `"read_view"`, `"configure_view"`,
  `"manage_layout"`, `"read_docs"`, `"execute_code"`, `"read_data"`.
  Omitted, all but `"execute_code"` and `"read_data"` are granted;
  `["read_view", "read_docs"]` yields a read-only agent. Users may
  switch granted entitlements off from the chat panel, never on.

# JavaScript Examples

```javascript
import { providers } from "@perspective-dev/viewer";

viewer.agentConfig({
    ...providers.anthropic,
    apiKey: "sk-ant-...",
    docs: fetch(
        "node_modules/@perspective-dev/viewer/dist/docs/perspective-docs.json",
    ),
});
```

members.name: agentPrompt
members.description:
Run one conversational turn of the embedded LLM agent (configured via
`agentConfig()`), resolving with the agent's final text response after
any tool calls have been applied to this element. Turns share a
conversation history (and the chat sidebar's transcript) until
`agentReset()`; a call made while a turn is already running rejects.
Tool activity is emitted as `perspective-agent-tool` CustomEvents on
this element. A failed turn rejects with an `Error` whose `retry()`
method retries it, returning a `Promise` that settles like this one.

# JavaScript Examples

```javascript
await viewer.agentPrompt("Show me sales by region as a bar chart");
```

members.name: agentReset
members.description:
Clear the agent's conversation (history and chat transcript), keeping
its configuration. Cancels any in-flight turn.

members.name: openTablePanel
members.description: Open or select a panel for a configured table using its retained panel configuration or defaults.

members.name: openChannel
members.description: Compatibility alias for openTablePanel().

members.name: showTable
members.description: Select an existing detail panel for a table or open one from its configured defaults, replacing filter clauses only on supplied columns. Preserves other panels and split proportions. Resolves to the selected panel ID through the lifecycle queue.

members.name: closeTablePanels
members.description: Close every panel for a table, including master panels, retaining one last panel configuration per table.

members.name: closeChannel
members.description: Compatibility alias for closeTablePanels().

members.name: restorePanel
members.description: Apply a partial viewer configuration to one existing panel through the lifecycle queue. Rejects unknown panel IDs and invalid configurations.

members.name: savePortableWorkspace
members.description: Compatibility alias for saveWorkspace().

members.name: saveClean
members.description: Compatibility alias for save(), writing legacy closed_channels metadata.
